title: Dino Danny and the dinosaurs.
lines: Danny is a six-year-old boy and he's crazy about dinosaurs.
He has a dinosaur on his pyjamas, a dinosaur on his cup and twenty plastic dinosaurs in a big box.
Today Danny is going to the museum with his class.
The big natural history museum in Brussels.
There are real dinosaur skeletons there.
On the bus Miss Ellen asks: Who knows how long ago the dinosaurs lived?
A very, very long time ago!
Then they arrive at the museum.
Inside it's a bit dark and very high.
It's as big as a house.
It has a long neck and a long tail.
Almost, says a man in a green jumper.
This is a diplodocus, a relative of the brontosaurus.
It had a very long neck, so it could eat leaves from the tallest trees.
It was big, but very gentle.
It had three horns on its head, and a big frill of bone around its neck.
It used that to protect itself.
It ate plants too, just like a cow.
And this one here, says Jonas in a deep voice, is the king of the dinosaurs.
It stands on two strong legs.
It has a gigantic head with sharp teeth.
But its arms are very small.
It couldn't even scratch its nose with them.
T. rex ate meat, says Jonas.
That's why it had those sharp teeth.
Each tooth was as big as a banana!
Then Jonas takes them to a special room.
Bones are hidden in the sand.
He gives everyone a little brush and a little shovel.
With his brush he sweeps the sand away.
And there he sees something white.
Then Jonas teaches them one more thing.
Did you know that the dinosaurs still have relatives alive today?
The blackbirds in your garden and the chickens on the farm are distant cousins of the dinosaurs.
A pigeon is hopping on the grass.
At the end everyone may choose a little dinosaur in the shop.
On the bus back to school he holds it tightly.
Miss, he says, when I grow up I'll be a palaeontologist too.
I believe you, says Miss Ellen.
That evening Danny puts his new triceratops next to his bed.
And he dreams of long necks, big horns and tiny arms.
